items.title: Graduating into Disruption: Labor Market Outcomes for AI-Exposed College Majors
items.claim: Graduates from the most AI-exposed majors had lower initial employment and full-quarter earnings after ChatGPT's release, but the exposure-based design cannot rule out every coincident field-specific shock.

items.title: Do Job Postings Show Early Labor Market Effects of AI?
items.claim: Broad U.S. job-posting data provide little indication of a distinct AI-driven decline in labor demand since ChatGPT's release, despite slower overall hiring.

items.title: What Work Does Generative AI Do?
items.claim: U.S. worker survey data show widespread but shallow task-level AI use and demonstrate that occupational exposure is an incomplete proxy for adoption.

items.title: You’re (not) Hired: Artificial Intelligence and Early Career Hiring in the Quarterly Workforce Indicators
items.claim: Early-career hiring and employment declined relative to less-exposed industry-state cells after ChatGPT's launch; the paper identifies unresolved pandemic-era and exposure-related confounding.

items.title: The Microstructure of AI Diffusion: Evidence From Firms, Business Functions, and Worker Tasks
items.claim: In the late-2025 to early-2026 survey window, most AI-using firms reported task augmentation only and few reported an AI-related employment decrease.

items.title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI
items.claim: Danish linked records show task reorganization but no detectable earnings or recorded-hours effect larger than 2% over two years.

items.title: Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index of Occupational Exposure
items.claim: One in four workers globally are in occupations with some generative-AI exposure; this is a task-exposure estimate, not observed job loss.
